profile.name: Terrence Ye Yang
profile.title: AI Developer & Applied Researcher
profile.headline: Building AI systems that know the edge of their own knowledge.
profile.summary: Half academic, half engineering — agentic retrieval for high-accountability domains, benchmarking tools for local model runtimes, and small products that put people and evidence back in the loop.
about: I split my time between applied AI research and hands-on engineering — roughly half academic, half production. My work centers on retrieval and agent systems that need to be trustworthy in domains where a confident wrong answer is costly: banking, compliance, and technical documentation.

Alongside that, I build tools for measuring and understanding model behavior — local benchmark dashboards, evidence repositories, and small community products — because good research needs good instruments.

news.title: Merged in Tencent/WeKnora (#5955) — Scope Postgres HNSW Fallback Retries to SET LOCAL Failures
news.summary: Upstreamed a transaction error-propagation fix to Tencent/WeKnora's PostgreSQL/pgvector retriever (VectorRetrieve). Previously, HNSW compatibility retries were triggered by inspecting the final transaction error text — allowing a BEGIN, query, or COMMIT failure that mentioned an HNSW setting name to launch an unrelated fallback query and overwrite the real failure. PR #5955 restricts retry eligibility strictly to the two SET LOCAL failure paths while preserving rollback-before-retry and retrieval SQL semantics, backed by deterministic red/green SQL-mock regression tests.

news.title: bwxPixel v0.2.0 — Blackwell __dp4a Kernel, Split-Weight AVX2 Baseline & Memory-Hierarchy Benchmarks
news.summary: Rebuilt both the CUDA and CPU paths of bwxPixel (plus a multi-arch sm_75–sm_120 C ABI DLL) and measured them on an RTX 5080 + i7-14700KF while keeping L2-resident, cold-DRAM, and PCIe round-trip regimes strictly separate. Replacing a cache-thrashing 16 MB lookup table with a split-weight [77, 51, 29, 99] AVX2 vpmaddubsw kernel and non-temporal streaming stores lifted the CPU baseline up to 27.3× (760.9 GB/s in cache; 64.2 GB/s cold DDR5). On the GPU, 128-bit vectorized __dp4a + dual-pipe PRMT/ALU kernels sustain 902.2 GB/s (94.0% of GDDR7 peak) across a >512 MiB multi-buffer ring and 4.90 TB/s (8.47 µs at 4K) in hot L2 via CUDA Graph — verified bit-exact across all 16,777,216 RGB colors and unaligned ROI pointers.

projects.name: PossOnto
projects.description: An agentic RAG that navigates knowledge graphs instead of retrieving fixed chunks — built to know when the source doesn't support an answer, and to escalate rather than guess. Demonstrated on a fictional bank's dispute-resolution policy.

projects.name: AI-Z
projects.description: A desktop dashboard for measuring how local and cloud model runtimes handle repeatable text-generation workloads — time-to-first-token, tokens/sec, and system telemetry across LM Studio and Ollama.

projects.name: AICANNOT
projects.description: A community-driven catalog where anyone can ask what AI still can't do, and anyone can answer — built with server actions and rate-limited anti-abuse from day one.

projects.name: Human-Z
projects.description: A companion thread to AI-Z's benchmark work, tracking what remains distinctly human against the growing capability of machine runtimes.

projects.name: VLA
projects.description: Early-stage exploration into vision-language-action models — grounding perception and language in embodied action.

projects.name: EVO
projects.description: A public evidence repository supporting the EVO DNA Atlas — collecting and organizing genomic evidence for open review.

projects.name: ChipSpot Cloud
projects.description: The public edge of an AI-native technical sourcing tool for electronic components: a requirement becomes a sourcing list of exact part numbers, each bound to official QVL/AVL evidence — and when the platform identity is missing, it says so instead of guessing. A Cloudflare Worker serves the case browser and holds no keys; evidence, models, and the reasoning path stay on a separately operated local engine.

projects.name: OCC
projects.description: A reusable optical transport core for moving files through screen-to-camera links when cables, app handoffs, and local-network setup add friction. The v1.0 binary preview exposes a stable C ABI with erasure recovery, integrity verification, artifact provenance, and hardware-acceleration hooks; benchmark evidence keeps physical-device, simulator, and protocol-simulation claims separate.

projects.name: bwxPixel
projects.description: An ultra-low-latency RGBX/RGBA-to-grayscale library and standalone C ABI DLL for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs and x86-64 CPUs. Pairs 128-bit vectorized __dp4a + dual-pipe PRMT/ALU kernels (with automatic unaligned-ROI fallback) against an honest split-weight AVX2 + non-temporal CPU baseline — reporting hot-L2 (4.90 TB/s), multi-buffer cold GDDR7 (902.2 GB/s, 94% of peak), and PCIe end-to-end numbers separately, verified bit-exact across all 16,777,216 RGB colors.
